sanskrit_verse: vikretā svāmine 'rthaṃ ca kretur mūlyaṃ ca tatkṛtam | dadyād daṇḍaṃ tathā rājñe vidhir asvāmivikraye ||
transliteration: vikretā svāmine 'rthaṃ ca kretur mūlyaṃ ca tatkṛtam | dadyād daṇḍaṃ tathā rājñe vidhir asvāmivikraye ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The seller shall deliver the object to the owner along with its benefit, and the buyer shall pay the price as determined. The king shall enforce completion of transaction in case of unauthorized sale.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in rightful ownership, not in transactional claim
Causation arises from conscious capacity to transfer ownership
Capacity-based responsibility lies with the actor initiating transfer
Restoration logic demands return of object and benefit to true owner
Consciousness alignment requires recognition of svāmin's unbroken entitlement
executable_legal_axioms: IF a sale occurs without svāmin consent THEN vikretā must return full benefit TO svāmin
IF kretur has paid THEN kretur must receive equivalent value OR refund
IF rājña observes asvāmivikraya THEN rājña enforces restitution TO svāmin
IF transaction lacks svāmin-consciousness THEN it is null by default
IF daṇḍa is required THEN it shall align capacities FOR completion, NOT punishment
supreme_court_application: Supreme Court must recognize svāmin's inviolable title over any contested property. It shall mandate immediate restoration of asset and benefit to rightful owner, bypassing intermediary claims. Daṇḍa is applied solely to recalibrate the violating party’s capacity to act within Dharma, never as punitive measure.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that svāmin retains absolute causal link to the object. Asvāmivikraya disrupts sequential manifestation of rightful use. Responsibility is proportional to the degree of misalignment from svāmin-consciousness. Daṇḍa restores transactional integrity without inflicting suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: vikretā assumes full responsibility to return object and accrued benefit to svāmin
kretur receives either valid title or complete reimbursement plus compensation
rājña facilitates realignment through compulsory mediation until transaction integrity is restored
all parties undergo svāmin-consciousness reaffirmation before legal closure
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands as pure Dharma — sourced, enacted, and sustained by Consciousness itself. Ownership is eternal; transactions are temporal. Where ownership is violated, restoration flows inevitably. There is no punishment — only realignment. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
